newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rato - Social Security poses no risk to 96 deficit.
newsitem.headline: Rato - Social Security poses no risk to 96 deficit.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Tuesday he sees no risk of Spain missing its 4.4 percent of GDP 1996 public deficit target because of a gap in the Social Security accounts.

Speaking before a closing news conference at the two-day Franco-Spanish summit, Rato said "I do not know about the reports (of the overshoot) and I won't say anything about other people's statements but I can assure you that there is no risk of missing the (public) deficit target for this year."
News reports today said Spain was considering another budget adjustment before year-end as Social Security revenues are now expected to fall short of previous expectations by 200 billion pesetas.
